spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.1 (flags: STREAM_START on the first datagram)
description: Baseline media datagrams with every header field exercised: STREAM_START on sequence 0 / timestamp 0, then the next datagram with all fields advanced. Payload = 8 stereo F32LE sample frames (64 B).
preconditions: Session PLAYING; instance 1, generation 1; 48 kHz stereo F32LE (8 bytes per sample frame).
Datagrams ride QUIC DATAGRAM; the bytes below are the full application payload (24-byte header + payload), NOT length-prefixed.
Payload bytes are a synthetic ramp (byte i = (start + i) mod 256) — audio content is irrelevant to framing; determinism is the point.

steps.note: First datagram of the instance: sequence 0, timestamp 0, STREAM_START set.
Next datagram: sequence +1, timestamp = prev + 8 frames (gapless continuity, §7.2), no flags.

assertions: Every header field is exercised across the two datagrams: instance 1, generation 1, sequence 0->1, timestamp 0->8, flags 0x1->0x0.
All header integers are big-endian (network byte order) — unlike protobuf's little-endian fixed64 — see the header table in protos/wire-protocol-v2/control.proto.
Timestamp counts SAMPLE FRAMES (stereo frame = one frame, never interleaved samples); continuity: ts(next) = ts(prev) + frames(prev) (§7.2).
STREAM_START is an anchor hint on sequence 0/timestamp 0; the instance and generation fields are authoritative (§7.1).
